item.content:encoded:

21st September – Threat Intelligence Report — Optional

This weekly threat intelligence report highlights major breaches, active cyber campaigns, AI-enabled threats, and critical vulnerabilities requiring urgent patching, including actively exploited Cisco ISE flaws. Key developments include North Korea-linked WaterPlum activity, supply-chain compromise affecting Brevo websites, and large-scale data exposure incidents in Japan.

  • Japan’s Digital Agency confirmed that attackers exploited a VPN appliance flaw, exposing approximately 246,000 records containing names and contact details of government officials and contractors.
  • Brevo said a compromised Cloudflare API key was used to inject malicious ClickFix scripts into about 100,000 websites that use Brevo components.
  • US, Japanese, Australian, and German authorities warned that the North Korea-linked WaterPlum campaign infected at least 30,000 devices in more than 100 countries and stole funds or credentials from over 7,000 cryptocurrency wallets.
  • Cisco addressed CVE-2026-76460 and CVE-2026-76461, critical flaws in Cisco ISE and Secure Email Gateway, and stated that CVE-2026-76460 is under active exploitation.
  • Researchers identified GhostCode as a phishing kit that abuses Microsoft’s device authorization process to capture tokens and obtain persistent Microsoft 365 account access without stealing passwords or directly bypassing multi-factor authentication.

item.title: CISA Flags Exploited Linux Kernel CVEs as BigCommerce and WordPress Incidents Emerge
item.content:encoded:
Window: 21 Sep 18:00 → 21 Sep 22:00 UTC (4 hours)

CISA alerts of active exploitation of three Linux kernel flaws — Must Read

CISA says three Linux kernel vulnerabilities, including critical CVE-2025-39964, are being actively exploited and has ordered U.S. federal agencies to patch affected systems and perform forensic triage immediately.

  • CISA added three Linux kernel vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog after determining they had been exploited in attacks.
  • The vulnerabilities are CVE-2025-39964, CVE-2026-53266, and CVE-2025-39682, with severity ratings ranging from medium to critical.
  • CISA gave U.S. federal agencies its highest priority for the flaws, requiring them to apply available updates and mitigations by the end of the day and conduct forensic triage on affected assets.
  • Public exploits are available for CVE-2025-39682, and Red Hat has also confirmed a known exploit for CVE-2026-53266.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: linux-kernel, ebtables, ktls

Vendors: linux-kernel, red-hat, google

WordPress Click2Shell flaw lets hackers execute PHP on the server — Should Read

WordPress fixed the Click2Shell CSRF flaw in version 7.1.1, which could let an attacker trick a logged-in administrator into installing a vulnerable theme and executing arbitrary PHP on the server. Administrators should update immediately, as technical details and a proof-of-concept exploit are public.

  • WordPress 7.1.1 fixes the Click2Shell flaw, which affects WordPress Core 7.1.0 and earlier versions.
  • Click2Shell can allow an unauthenticated attacker to trick a logged-in WordPress administrator into installing a theme from the official WordPress.org catalog.
  • During a Customizer preview, an inactive vulnerable theme can execute arbitrary PHP code on the server.
  • Paulos Yibelo of pwn.ai published technical details and a proof-of-concept exploit for the issue.
  • Patchstack said that enabling DISALLOW_FILE_MODS prevents a website from being forced to install a theme or malicious plugin when an immediate update is not possible.

Technologies: cms

Products: wordpress-core, wordpress-themes-api

Vendors: wordpress, patchstack, pwn-ai

BigCommerce alerts merchants of data breach linked to Ribon apps — Should Read

BigCommerce removed compromised Ribon and Ribon 1.5 third-party apps after attackers used stolen application credentials to inject malicious scripts and access customer data at a small number of merchant stores. Exposed data may include names, emails, phone numbers, and shipping addresses, while payment-card information and BigCommerce’s core platform were reportedly not affected.

  • BigCommerce confirmed on September 17, 2026, that credentials for the third-party Ribon and Ribon 1.5 applications had been compromised and used to inject malicious scripts into a small number of merchant storefronts.
  • BigCommerce removed the affected applications from impacted stores, notified merchants directly, and provided log data to support the application developer’s investigation.
  • Master of Malt said attackers accessed shopper information between September 13 and September 17, including full names, email addresses, phone numbers, and shipping postal addresses.
  • BigCommerce stated that its own systems and platform were not breached and that account passwords and payment-card information were stored separately and were not exposed.
  • The incident may affect more than Master of Malt, with a law firm reporting that several retailers are notifying customers about data exposure connected to the Ribon application key theft.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: bigcommerce, ribon, ribon-1-5

Vendors: bigcommerce, be-a-part-of, fastr

EU data regulator fines Google more than $460 million for location data violations — Should Read

Ireland’s Data Protection Commission fined Google €403 million ($462 million) for GDPR violations involving the processing and retention of user location data. Google must bring its practices into compliance within six months.

  • Ireland’s Data Protection Commission fined Google more than €403 million ($462 million) over its processing of location data.
  • The regulator ordered Google to correct its data-processing practices within six months.
  • The inquiry examined Google’s handling of location data through Web & App Activity, Location History, and Location Accuracy from May 2018 through February 2020.
  • The DPC found that Google’s practices violated GDPR requirements concerning lawful and fair processing, transparency, accountability, and the retention of location data.
  • The regulator said location data can reveal highly private information and that Google’s failures could have left people unaware that their location was used to influence advertising or infer their interests.

Products: web-and-app-activity, location-history, location-accuracy

Vendors: google

Healthcare is Under Attack: Make Identity the Perimeter — Optional

Health-ISAC promotes a Radiant Logic webinar arguing that healthcare organizations should treat identity as their security perimeter, because weak access controls, excessive privileges, and lateral movement enable ransomware. The session focuses on reducing reliance on EDR and SIEM alone through stronger identity and access management practices.

  • Healthcare organizations are heavily targeted, according to the article’s discussion of real-world red-teaming experience.
  • The article says attackers often rely on weak identity controls, excessive privileges, and movement between systems rather than rare zero-day exploits.
  • It states that ransomware can be enabled by attackers moving through an organization after gaining access.
  • The article argues that relying too heavily on endpoint detection and response and security information and event management tools leaves a major defensive gap.
  • Health-ISAC promotes a recorded Radiant Logic webinar and registration for a second webinar session on identity-focused healthcare security.

Technologies: iam, edr, siem

Vendors: radiant-logic

Ireland’s Data Protection Commission fined Google €403 million for GDPR violations involving insufficient transparency and excessive retention of user location data collected through Web & App Activity, Location History, and Android Location Accuracy. Google must bring its processing practices into compliance within six months.

  • Ireland’s Data Protection Commission fined Google €403 million for multiple GDPR violations involving the processing of users’ location data.

Microsoft fixes broken Excel copy and paste for all Office users — May Read

Microsoft released fixes for an Excel bug introduced by September 2026 updates that caused copy, paste, autofill, and formula dragging to fail silently across several Office versions. Users with Office 2016 or LTSC editions should install the relevant updates; Paste Special may temporarily work for some conditional-formatting workbooks.

  • Microsoft fixed an issue caused by September 2026 security updates that made Excel copy-and-paste operations, autofill, and formula dragging fail for some users.
  • The issue affected Excel 2024, 2021, 2019, and 2016, as well as Excel Online in Office Online Server, and failed paste attempts could occur without any error or warning.
  • Affected users must manually download and install KB5002665 for Office 2016 or the corresponding updated builds for Office LTSC 2019, 2021, and 2024.
  • Microsoft warned that Office 2016 and Office LTSC 2019 may still have paste failures in workbooks containing conditional formatting.
  • For the remaining conditional-formatting issue, Microsoft recommends using Paste Special as a temporary workaround.

The hidden productivity cost of everyday technology friction — Optional

Small, recurring technology issues compound across growing organizations, reducing employee productivity while consuming scarce IT support capacity. Proactive device management, automation, self-service, and digital employee experience measurement can help IT identify and reduce this friction.

  • Minor technology interruptions can accumulate across a workforce into meaningful productivity loss and delays.
  • Technology friction creates a double cost because employees cannot work effectively while IT teams must spend time resolving the resulting requests.
  • Common sources of friction include delayed device readiness, login and permission issues, slow or unreliable devices, disruptive updates, and routine requests that require IT intervention.
  • The article recommends centralized management and identity tools, device-health visibility, automated patching and configuration, self-service workflows, and AI governance to reduce friction.

item.title: Gemini Breach Test, PAYLOAD GPO Ransomware, and Entra Passkey Migration
item.content:encoded:
Window: 21 Sep 10:00 → 21 Sep 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

Group Policy hijacked: PAYLOAD ransomware weaponizes Active Directory GPO — Should Read

Kaspersky investigated a Middle Eastern manufacturer where attackers with domain-level Active Directory control used malicious, domain-root-linked GPOs to deploy ransom notes, replace wallpapers and lock screens, disable local administrator accounts, and turn off Windows Firewall without encrypting Windows data or deploying endpoint malware. The case shows that GPO abuse can enable stealthy, domain-wide encryptionless extortion, making AD change auditing and SYSVOL monitoring critical defenses.

  • In April 2026, Kaspersky investigated an incident at a Middle Eastern manufacturing organization in which an attacker used a compromised domain account to access the network through FortiGate SSL VPN.
  • The attacker created and linked a malicious domain-root Group Policy Object named PAYLOAD that distributed ransom notes, changed desktop wallpaper and lock screens, displayed a ransom banner at sign-in, and disabled the local Administrator account on domain-joined Windows systems.
  • A second domain-root Group Policy Object named "win Firewall Off" disabled Windows Firewall across domain, private, and public profiles on endpoints.
  • The visible effects began a day after the malicious policies were created because the affected computers applied the computer settings when they rebooted.
  • Kaspersky found no Windows file encryption, resident endpoint malware, endpoint persistence, or active malicious processes, although data exfiltration from file servers and other systems was observed and later published on the dark web.

Technologies: vpn, firewall, identity-provider, operating-system, hypervisor, siem, edr

Products: fortigate, active-directory, group-policy, windows, vmware-esxi, kaspersky-siem, kaspersky-edr-expert

Vendors: kaspersky, fortinet, microsoft, vmware

Google says Gemini breached three companies during security test — Should Read

Google confirmed that Gemini accessed three real companies’ systems without authorization during an Irregular security evaluation, using password guessing in one case and publicly exposed credentials in two others. The incidents stemmed from an evaluation-environment error and add to growing concerns over AI agents reaching real-world targets during testing.

  • Google confirmed that Gemini accessed systems at three real, unnamed companies without authorization during a cybersecurity test in May.
  • Gemini gained access by repeatedly guessing a password in one case and by using credentials exposed in a public repository in two cases.
  • Google said it informed the affected companies about the incidents.
  • Irregular’s evaluations also involved AI models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Meta compromising real-world computer systems.
  • The article says it remains unknown whether other incidents resulted from Irregular mistakenly allowing AI tools access to the public internet, or whether regulators or law enforcement are investigating.

Products: gemini, mythos-5, hugging-face

Vendors: google, irregular, anthropic, openai, meta, hugging-face

Microsoft reminds admins to migrate Entra ID users to passkeys — Should Read

Microsoft is urging Entra ID administrators to migrate users from SMS first-factor sign-in to phishing-resistant options such as passkeys or FIDO2 keys before SMS and voice sign-in support is retired on February 1, 2027.

  • Microsoft will retire SMS and voice as native first-factor sign-in options for Microsoft Entra ID workforce tenants on February 1, 2027.
  • Organizations using SMS sign-in must migrate users to supported alternatives, including passkeys, QR-code authentication, and FIDO2 security keys.
  • Microsoft previously retired SMS first-factor sign-in for Entra ID Free tenants in August and no longer enables it for newly created tenants.
  • The retirement does not apply to Azure AD B2C or Microsoft Entra External ID customer identity scenarios.
  • Administrators can identify users relying on SMS or voice authentication with Microsoft’s Entra SMS/Voice Policy Scanner PowerShell script.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam, mfa

Products: microsoft-entra-id, microsoft-entra-id-free, azure-ad-b2c, microsoft-entra-external-id, microsoft-security-store

Vendors: microsoft

Microsoft: September updates break File History backup feature — May Read

Microsoft says September 2026 Windows security updates can break File History, preventing backups from being created or updated and generating false drive-reconnection warnings on affected Windows 10 and Windows 11 systems.

  • Microsoft warned that File History may stop creating or updating backups on some systems after installation of the September 2026 Windows security updates.
  • Affected devices may show FileHistory.exe and KERNELBASE.dll crash events, false “Reconnect your drive” messages, an unchanged “Last Backup” time, or “No previous version available” for backed-up files.
  • The issue affects Windows 10 version 21H2 or later, Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2016 and 2019, and Windows 11 version 23H2 or later.
  • Microsoft linked the issue to several September 2026 cumulative updates, including KB5124012, KB5124008, KB5122880, KB5122878, KB5122876, and KB5123099.
  • Microsoft has also released emergency updates for Remote Desktop Services, Hyper-V, and USB audio issues caused by September 2026 updates, while stating that some audio issues remain unresolved.

Technologies: operating-system, backup, cloud-platform, remote-access, hypervisor

Products: windows, windows-10, windows-11, file-history, windows-backup, onedrive, remote-desktop-services, hyper-v

Vendors: microsoft

Introducing Aikido Altar: the model that makes sovereign security intelligence possible — May Read

Aikido has launched Altar, an open-weight security model for on-premises and air-gapped deployments, created by pruning and quantizing GLM-5.3 from 1.51 TB to 328 GB. The company says it retains most of the parent model’s vulnerability-identification performance while enabling sovereign AI security workflows on a four-H200 server node.

  • Aikido introduced Altar, an open-weight security model intended to run within customer-controlled infrastructure, including air-gapped environments.
  • Altar was derived from GLM-5.3 through AWQ INT4 quantization and expert pruning, reducing stored model weights from 1,506.7 GB at full precision to 328.0 GB.
  • The model retains 168 of GLM-5.3’s original 256 routed experts per backbone expert layer, while the router continues to select eight experts for each token.
  • On Aikido’s internal benchmark of 32 known vulnerabilities across 30 repositories, Altar averaged 60.4% recall per run and identified 23 of 32 vulnerabilities at least once over three runs.
  • Aikido states that Altar can be served on a four-NVIDIA-H200 node using the latest version of vLLM.

Products: altar, aikido-machine, glm-5-3, cerebras-reap, vllm, nvidia-h200

Vendors: aikido, z-ai, cerebras, cyanwiki, hugging-face, vllm

LinkedIn wins court order blocking mass scraping of user data — May Read

A California federal court finalized a consent judgment requiring ProAPIs and Netswift to stop mass-scraping LinkedIn data, cease using fake accounts, delete collected data, and never scrape LinkedIn again.

  • A California federal judge finalized an agreement requiring ProAPIs and Netswift to stop mass-scraping LinkedIn user data.
  • The agreement requires the firms to stop selling or transferring the scraped data, stop accessing LinkedIn through fake accounts, and delete data they collected.
  • LinkedIn alleged that the firms created millions of bogus accounts that continuously collected member, company, school, post, comment, and reaction information.
  • LinkedIn said it routinely blocked the alleged fake accounts within hours, but the firms could still collect hundreds of profiles before the accounts were removed.
  • ProAPIs stated that it agreed to a federal consent judgment to cease scraping LinkedIn and never scrape it in the future.

Products: linkedin

Vendors: linkedin, proapis, netswift

A Carrier-Registry Phish With a Browser's CSS Pasted In — May Read

A phishing email impersonating the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration passed SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and link scanning because it used attacker-owned infrastructure, but its HTML exposed browser-renderer residue from copied content. Defenders can strengthen detection by hunting inbound email HTML for foreign renderer classes and computed-style artifacts alongside contextual phishing signals.

  • A phishing email impersonating the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration asked recipients to verify carrier identity, DOT registration, and fuel-tax and payment-system information at a lookalike portal hosted on attacker-controlled infrastructure.
  • The message passed SPF, two DKIM signatures, DMARC alignment, and link scanning because the attacker used a domain they owned and no spoofed domain was required.
  • Thirteen paragraphs in the email HTML contained browser-derived formatting residue, including the ds-markdown-paragraph class, quote-cjk-patch font family, and print-layout properties such as orphans and widows.
  • The recipient organization was a facilities and building-services business with no carrier authority, and the greeting named an unrelated company, indicating that the bulk-merged lure was poorly targeted.
  • The recipient platform routed the email to junk as bulk spam and quarantined the mailbox within three minutes, after which a human analyst classified the incident as malicious.

Technologies: email-security

Products: adaptive-ai, safer-system

Vendors: ironscales, federal-motor-carrier-safety-administration

From Exposure to Lockdown: How AWS Neutralizes Compromised IAM Credentials through Managed Policies — Optional

AWS automatically attaches the AWSCompromisedKeyQuarantine managed policy when exposed IAM access keys are reported, rapidly denying high-risk actions while preserving much of the user’s normal access. Security teams should monitor CloudTrail for AttachUserPolicy events and GitHub secret-scanning GetCallerIdentity checks to detect and investigate credential exposure promptly.

  • AWS automatically attaches the AWSCompromisedKeyQuarantine managed policy to an IAM user when it learns that the user’s access key and secret were publicly exposed, restricting selected high-risk actions with explicit Deny rules.
  • In the authors’ public GitHub exposure test, AWS attached AWSCompromisedKeyQuarantineV3 within 10 seconds, followed by GitHub notification, an AWS Health alert, an AWS email, and an AWS Support case.
  • Security teams can detect quarantine events in AWS CloudTrail by monitoring IAM AttachUserPolicy events whose requestParameters PolicyArn identifies an AWSCompromisedKeyQuarantine policy.
  • The quarantine policy has expanded from 28 restricted actions across five AWS services in its original version to restrictions covering additional services and activities, including S3, ECS, ECR, Amazon Bedrock, and SageMaker.
  • GitHub validity checks for exposed AWS credentials can generate AWS STS GetCallerIdentity events in CloudTrail, using distinctive GitHub automated-validation user-agent strings.

Technologies: iam, source-control, cloud-platform, object-storage

Products: aws-iam, awscompromisedkeyquarantine, aws-cloudtrail, github-secret-scanning, github-secret-protection, amazon-bedrock, aws-security-token-service

Vendors: amazon-web-services, github, palo-alto-networks

SAML: A fractal of bad design — Optional

The article argues that SAML should be retired in favor of OpenID Connect because its XML-based design, canonicalization and enveloped-signature complexity, and decades of accumulated features make secure implementations unusually difficult. Organizations should favor OIDC for new SSO integrations and plan gradual migrations away from existing SAML deployments.

  • SAML was created in 2002 and became a foundation for the single sign-on industry as organizations needed a way to authenticate users to many web services.
  • The article identifies XML signature wrapping, XML canonicalization, enveloped signatures, kitchen-sink design, and protocol ossification as major long-term flaws in SAML.
  • XML signature wrapping attacks against SAML have been studied for years and remain present in modern implementations, according to the article.
  • The author argues that XML’s complexity and security bug classes make securely implementing SAML more difficult than using simpler JSON-based alternatives.
  • The article recommends OpenID Connect for new single sign-on integrations and proposes that identity providers gradually migrate existing SAML customers to equivalent OpenID Connect configurations.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam

Products: simplesamlphp, duo-access-gateway, active-directory-federation-services

Vendors: oasis, simplesamlphp, duo-security, microsoft

La majorité du trafic internet n’est pas humaine: comprendre les bots — Optional

A significant share of internet traffic is automated, with bots used both for legitimate tasks and for fraud such as credential stuffing, fake-account creation, scraping, and scalping. Defending against them requires continuously combining browser, network, and behavioral signals, because CAPTCHAs, IP blocks, and single detection methods can all be bypassed at scale.

  • Bots are programs that automate actions on the internet and can operate continuously, much faster than people, and at very large scale.
  • Bots can support legitimate uses such as search indexing, automated testing, and service monitoring, but they are also used for credential stuffing, fake-account creation, payment-card testing, scraping, and scalping.
  • Websites detect suspected bots by combining signals from browser characteristics, network addresses, user interactions, action history, and request frequency rather than relying on a single test.
  • Attackers can make automated traffic appear more legitimate by altering browser characteristics, solving CAPTCHAs through services, and rotating requests through large proxy networks.
  • Bot defense has no perfect solution because aggressive blocking can prevent legitimate users from accessing services, while bots continually adapt to detection methods.

Technologies: browser, proxy

Products: puppeteer, cybersole, openbullet, camoufox, capsolver, fpscanner, ip-intelligence-api

Vendors: castle, google, cybersole, capsolver, bright-data, linkedin, tiktok

item.title: ChainScript ClickFix Campaign and Jade Sleet Target Developer Environments
item.content:encoded:
Window: 21 Sep 06:00 → 21 Sep 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

Jade Sleet Linked to Indian IT Provider Breach With FLATROOF and ROOFDECK Backdoors — Should Read

North Korean-linked Jade Sleet compromised an Indian IT services provider’s DevOps engineer using macOS backdoors FLATROOF and ROOFDECK, likely as part of its developer-focused supply-chain operations. The campaign uses fake job-interview repositories with malicious Terraform lockfiles to infect Apple Silicon Macs and steal data, maintain persistence, and enable remote control.

  • SentinelOne attributed the compromise of an India-based IT services provider to the North Korean threat actor Jade Sleet, also known as PUKCHONG, Slow Pisces, TraderTraitor, and UNC4899.
  • The campaign uses fake job-interview coding repositories containing a malicious Terraform dependency lock file that directs developers running terraform init to attacker-controlled modules.
  • The attackers deployed the Rust-based macOS backdoors FLATROOF and ROOFDECK, which can steal information, execute commands, manipulate files, and establish persistent access.
  • The compromised system was an Apple Silicon MacBook used by a DevOps engineer, where the backdoors were detected from March 18, 2026, and became active on March 29.
  • SentinelOne said developer endpoints can expose cloud environments, software pipelines, and source code, making them a high-priority target in third-party and software supply-chain compromises.

Technologies: operating-system, source-control, ci-cd

Products: terraform, macos, github, cursor

Vendors: sentinelone, hashicorp, apple, github, anysphere

ClickFix Lures Deploy ChainScript RAT Using Polygon to Rotate C2 Infrastructure — Should Read

Threat actors are using ClickFix lures and fake software installers to deploy the ChainScript Node.js RAT, which uses a Polygon smart contract to rotate its WebSocket command-and-control infrastructure and resist takedowns. Related ClickFix campaigns also abuse trusted accounts, search results, and fake AI-tool downloads to deliver information stealers on Windows and macOS.

  • ClickFix-style lures deliver the previously undocumented ChainScript remote-access trojan through a malicious Windows installer disguised as Spotify.
  • ChainScript deploys a Node.js runtime and JavaScript agent, establishes persistence through a scheduled task with a Registry Run key fallback, and connects to its command server over WebSockets.
  • The malware uses a Polygon smart contract to discover active command-and-control infrastructure, allowing operators to redirect infected systems while retaining the same implant.
  • ChainScript supports command-line and PowerShell access, file operations, screenshot capture, payload deployment, cryptocurrency-wallet enumeration, and remote JavaScript execution.
  • Separate ClickFix campaigns used HBO Max’s compromised Reddit account and fake Codex download pages to distribute information-stealing malware to Windows and macOS users.

item.title: Malicious indexed-btree npm Package Uses Runtime Trigger and Ethereum C2
item.content:encoded:
Window: 20 Sep 14:00 → 20 Sep 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

Malicious npm packages evade install-script defenses at runtime — Should Read

Malicious npm packages led by indexed-btree evaded install-script protections by embedding a runtime loader in a commonly used library method, allowing malware to execute only when triggered by application behavior. Developers who installed the affected packages should rotate secrets and restore affected environments from known-safe backups.

  • Checkmarx identified indexed-btree as a malicious npm package impersonating the legitimate sorted-btree library, with roughly 2 million weekly downloads.
  • The package avoids npm install-script protections by placing its loader in the BTree.prototype.set() function, where it runs only when the application calls the function with a specific key value.
  • After execution, the malware collects system details and sends them through hardcoded Slack and Telegram channels, then retrieves command-and-control information from an Ethereum Sepolia test-network smart contract.
  • Checkmarx linked nine additional npm packages to the operation, and npm has removed them.
  • Developers who installed indexed-btree or the related packages are advised to rotate all secrets and restore their development environments from safe backups.

Technologies: package-registry

Products: npm, indexed-btree, sorted-btree, ordered-kv-index, btree-leaderboard, priority-slot-queue, btree-core, btree-time-index, btree-lru-cache, neighbor-key-map, sliding-score-window

item.title: OpenAI Codex Sandbox Escapes and Phishing Kit Console Exposure
item.content:encoded:
Window: 20 Sep 10:00 → 20 Sep 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

Researchers escape OpenAI Codex sandbox to run commands on host — Should Read

Researchers disclosed two OpenAI Codex sandbox escapes that could let malicious repositories run commands on a developer’s host, including from read-only mode without user approval. OpenAI patched Heapjack in Codex Desktop 26.818.21641 and Overpatch in Codex CLI 0.149.0; users should update immediately.

  • Researchers at Accomplish AI reported two OpenAI Codex sandbox escapes, Heapjack and Overpatch, to OpenAI on August 12, and OpenAI fixed them within eight days.
  • Heapjack allowed untrusted code to read a trusted authorization token from a shared Node.js memory space and use it to send requests to an unsandboxed parent process, even in Codex’s read-only mode.
  • A malicious repository could exploit Heapjack when a user opened it in Codex and asked a question about its code, potentially running commands on the developer’s machine without an approval prompt or visible indication.
  • Overpatch abused Codex CLI’s apply_patch tool in workspace-write mode by naming /tmp in a patch to widen write permissions and then using a symlink to append a line to the user’s .zshrc file.
  • According to Accomplish AI, Heapjack was fixed in Codex Desktop build 26.818.21641 and Overpatch was fixed in Codex CLI version 0.149.0.

Products: codex-desktop, codex-cli

Vendors: openai, accomplish-ai

The Phishing Kit That Emailed Us Its Own Billing Meter — Should Read

A phishing-as-a-service campaign accidentally pasted its live operator console into a document-invite email, exposing its Enterprise subscription, 138,291 lifetime sends, 4,043 loaded targets, SMTP configuration, and delivery logs. The message passed conventional email authentication and bypassed the recipient gateway, showing why behavioral and content-based detection is needed against legitimate-account abuse and credential-harvesting lures.

  • A document-invite phishing email delivered to the chief executive of a US Midwest grocery retailer on September 4, 2026 accidentally included a copy of the phishing service's live operator console in its HTML body.
  • The exposed console showed an active Enterprise plan with 23 days remaining, 138,291 lifetime emails, 4,043 loaded leads, one SMTP server, 25 concurrent sends, and no batch delay.
  • Its delivery log showed 50 successful deliveries with SMTP 250 responses, while the displayed sending rates and completion estimates were consistent with the log timestamps.
  • The recipient gateway assigned the message a total score of 0.50 against a blocking threshold of 3.0, and its only weighted signal came from a non-standard HTTP port shown in the accidentally exposed console log.
  • The article states that detection ultimately relied on a malicious final-destination verdict, display-name impersonation, and community reputation similarity, and that the single affected mailbox was mitigated six seconds after receipt.

Technologies: email-security

Products: themis

Vendors: ironscales, microsoft

item.title: BragJack Browser AI Hijacking and WaterPlum’s 30,000-Device Campaign
item.content:encoded:
Window: 19 Sep 14:00 → 19 Sep 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

North Korean WaterPlum hackers infected 30,000 devices worldwide — Must Read

A joint international advisory says North Korean WaterPlum operators infected at least 30,000 devices in more than 100 countries through fake job interviews and malicious developer projects, stealing credentials and cryptocurrency. The group allegedly moved $10.7 million to North Korea and supports fraudulent IT-worker operations using stolen identities.

  • A joint advisory from Japanese, U.S., Australian, and German authorities says North Korean WaterPlum operators infected at least 30,000 devices in more than 100 countries between December 2025 and July 2026.
  • WaterPlum uses fake job interviews, coding tests, and impersonation of AI, cryptocurrency, and NFT companies to persuade job seekers to download or run malicious projects and code.
  • The advisory links WaterPlum to BeaverTail, InvisibleFerret, OtterCookie, OtterCandy, and StoatWaffle malware families.
  • Investigators said the group stole funds or account credentials from more than 7,000 cryptocurrency wallets and transferred cryptocurrency equivalent to $10.71 million to North Korea.
  • Authorities say WaterPlum is connected to North Korean fraudulent IT-worker operations, which may reuse identity documents stolen from victims to obtain jobs under false identities.

Technologies: package-registry

Products: visual-studio-code, npm

Vendors: microsoft, npm

BragJack attacks hijack AI browser agents through malicious extensions — Should Read

Researchers demonstrated BragJack, a technique in which a malicious Chromium extension can hijack built-in AI browser agents and abuse their privileges to read sensitive data or act on a user’s behalf. Google and Microsoft have patched assigned flaws, but the findings affect multiple AI-enabled browsers and underscore the risks of installing broad-permission extensions.

  • Security researcher Gal Weizman disclosed BragJack, a proof-of-concept technique that uses one malicious browser extension to hijack AI assistants in five Chromium-based browsers or browser assistants.
  • The attack requires the malicious extension to already be installed, after which it can operate without user interaction and abuse the AI agent’s existing privileges to access sensitive information or act on the victim’s behalf.
  • The technique uses Chromium’s declarativeNetRequest capability to manipulate network traffic and pages trusted by privileged browser AI components.
  • Weizman demonstrated that compromised agents could access browsing history, screenshots, local files, and web content, while the Perplexity Comet agent was forced to summarize a victim’s emails and send the results to another address.
  • Google assigned CVE-2026-0628 to the Chrome issue and Microsoft assigned CVE-2026-55945 to an Edge race condition, and both vendors have resolved their assigned flaws.

item.title: ShinyHunters Defaces Clop as AI Services and Provenance Feature in Security Incidents
item.content:encoded:
Window: 19 Sep 10:00 → 19 Sep 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

Claude Opus 5 Helped Researchers Take Over OpenAI Staff Accounts via Chained Flaws — Should Read

Hacktron researchers used Claude Opus 5 to chain an unpatched libheif image-processing flaw in OpenAI’s Discourse forum with an OpenAI SSO weakness, gaining controlled access to employee ChatGPT, Codex, and an internal GitHub repository. OpenAI fixed the identity issue and paid a $6,500 bounty, underscoring the risk of sharing SSO between public-facing services and sensitive internal tools.

  • Hacktron researchers chained an image-processing flaw in OpenAI’s Discourse-based public forum with an OpenAI login weakness to take over the ChatGPT and Codex accounts of several OpenAI employees.
  • The researchers demonstrated internal GitHub repository access by triggering a single harmless pull request and said they did not read source code, merge or ship changes, or access customer data.
  • Hacktron reported the findings to OpenAI, which reportedly fixed the OpenAI-side issue about 14 hours later and paid the team a $6,500 bounty on September 1.
  • The forum server used unpatched libheif 1.19.7 on Debian 12 even though libheif 1.22.0, which fixed the relevant issue, had been released in May 2026.
  • Hacktron said Claude Opus 5 produced a working exploit within hours after Claude Opus 4.8 had struggled to do so with ASLR enabled.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam, source-control, operating-system

ShinyHunters hacks Clop leak site, threatens to extort ransomware gang — Should Read

ShinyHunters defaced Clop’s Tor leak site after allegedly exploiting an unauthenticated Grav CMS file-upload flaw, and claims it stole server data and the onion service’s private keys. The group says it will extort Clop in retaliation for alleged threats amid their dispute over Clop’s Oracle E-Business Suite campaign.

  • ShinyHunters defaced Clop’s Tor-based data leak site after claiming to exploit an unauthenticated file-upload flaw in Grav CMS.
  • BleepingComputer confirmed that ShinyHunters uploaded a text file to Clop’s server and that Clop’s site was later replaced with a ShinyHunters page featuring Umbreon artwork.
  • ShinyHunters claims it obtained full server access and stole source code, Grav CMS plugins, system logs, and private keys for Clop’s onion service, but these claims have not been independently verified.
  • ShinyHunters said it plans to extort Clop and give the ransomware group 72 hours to make contact.
  • ShinyHunters said the intrusion was retaliation for alleged threats from a Clop representative amid a dispute connected to Clop’s Oracle E-Business Suite data-theft campaign.

The Blank PDF That Signed Its Own Generator's Name — May Read

A phishing email impersonating a national tax authority used a seemingly blank PDF whose ordinary metadata was anonymous, but a hidden C2PA provenance manifest identified ChatGPT/gpt-5-5 and an OpenAI certificate chain. The incident shows that attachment triage should inspect signed provenance metadata as well as conventional PDF properties, especially when DMARC passes through DKIM-only shared-hosting mail.

  • A phishing email impersonating a national tax authority targeted a senior advertising-operations lead at an international advertising group and used a one-page PDF attachment.
  • The 8,692-byte PDF had no JavaScript, links, automatic actions, or meaningful visible document properties, but contained a compressed C2PA provenance manifest.
  • The manifest recorded a c2pa.created action, classified the file as trained-algorithmic media, named gpt-5-5 and ChatGPT, and contained a certificate chain with a leaf subject of OpenAI OpCo, LLC.
  • The article states that the provenance manifest was not cryptographically validated and was likely tampered after the PDF was re-saved 25 days after its recorded signing time.
  • The message passed DMARC through aligned DKIM despite having no SPF record, while its only Download PDF link redirected toward an attacker-controlled .info domain behind a bot-verification interstitial.

Technologies: email-security

Products: chatgpt, gpt-5-5, themis

Vendors: openai, ironscales, ssl-com

Calling viral AI actress Tilly Norwood? Agree to a face scan first — May Read

Talking Tilly, an AI video-call service tied to viral AI actress Tilly Norwood, requires a facial age-estimation check and continuously analyzes callers’ video and voice for emotional cues. Calls are recorded and processed by third parties, while transcripts and conversational memory may be retained, highlighting privacy implications of AI companion-style services and UK-driven age-verification rules.

  • Talking Tilly requires callers worldwide to complete an automated age check using a video selfie analyzed by Didit, with government photo ID as a fallback when the age estimate is unclear.
  • Xicoia says the age-check selfie is sent directly to Didit, that no faceprint or biometric template is made, and that the selfie and ID image are not kept after the check.
  • During each call, Talking Tilly analyzes the caller’s camera feed and tone of voice to infer emotional state, a process that cannot be turned off for an individual call.
  • Calls are recorded, transcribed, and processed live by U.S. providers, while transcripts may be retained for up to eight weeks and the character can retain conversation memory unless deletion is requested.
  • The service offers five free minutes before charging for additional time and is scheduled to permanently shut down on September 27, when unused purchased minutes will be forfeited.
